# ml-keywords — the ML trigger word list (generated mirror)

**Do not edit this file by hand.** It is generated from `lib/ml-keywords.json`, which is the
single source of truth. `scripts/selftest.mjs` asserts that the JSON source, the embedded
fallback inside `router-planner-core.mjs`, and this mirror all carry the **same term set**.

Counts: **118 strong terms** (66 zh, 52 en) and **19 ambiguous entries**.

## How the trigger works

The list is **orthogonal** to the behaviour band. Matching it does not change the band and does
not replace the band's guidance; it appends a compact ML block to whatever guidance the band
already chose. That is what keeps the existing router behaviour byte-identical.

**Guard rule.**

- Enter ML detection only when at least **1 `terms` entry matches**.
- A text matching **only** `ambiguous` entries never changes the band. It may append a soft
  one-line hint to the existing band guidance, nothing more.
- '≥2' always means a count of **different ambiguous patterns**, and each pattern counts at most
  **once per text** — never by number of occurrences.

Latin patterns are word-boundary anchored and case-insensitive. Chinese patterns are literal
substrings chosen so that they are not contained in common unrelated words.

## Known traps this list is built to avoid

| Trap | Handling |
|---|---|
| `shap` matching `shape` / `reshape` / `shaping` | word-boundary anchored: `\bshap\b` |
| `model` / `feature` / `loss` in ordinary engineering prose | classified **ambiguous**, never sufficient alone |
| Chinese `回归` in the sense of *regression testing* | classified **ambiguous** |
| Chinese `分类` inside an unrelated word | classified **ambiguous** |
| A term appearing in both lists | forbidden; a duplicate check runs over both lists |

## Measured discriminating power

Fixtures live in `scripts/fixtures/ml-band-cases.json` (10 positive, 7 negative) and were
measured when the list was frozen: **false-trigger rate 0.0 %** on the negatives and **hit rate
100 %** on the positives, with the `shape` / `reshape` / `modeling` / `classify` substring
probes all non-matching. Recall is reported alongside precision deliberately: an earlier revision
scored 0 % false triggers but only 70 % recall, because `R²` (the superscript character) and a
bare `SHAP` were missing.
